## V9.7 — 30 July 2026

Delta over V9.6 — the third batch of the same day. **Van filters on Schedule and Reports**, which surfaced that one column had been quietly doing two incompatible jobs. **A stale-props class found in the component that had been patching around it three times.** **URL persistence for the dashboard's event and tab.** **Server-confirmed writes**, and a definitive answer to a staleness question flagged twice. **The realtime publication turned out to contain two tables, not three — one subscription had never fired.** Settings-card conventions settled. **No new columns. Still no Stripe: company setup is on hold pending outside factors.**

- **🔴 `orders.van_id` IS A KDS ROUTING FIELD AND CANNOT CARRY ACCOUNTING MEANING.** Live on test-truck: **51 of 65 orders (78%) have `van_id = NULL` while their event is assigned to a van.** The walk-up path never sets it; the customer path sets it from the event row — which is precisely why it works as a walk-up discriminator, and precisely why it cannot be summed. A Reports filter keyed on it would have shown Van1's revenue as ~£300 of a real £1,447, and the sum across vans would not have reconciled to the truck total. **A column that is inconsistently populated ON PURPOSE cannot be given a second purpose that requires consistency.** Same family as `channel` vs `method`.

- **THE FILTER SELECTS EVENTS, NOT ORDERS.** The settled model: a van filter chooses which **events** a report covers, and every order belonging to a selected event is included whole. Nothing is apportioned. That retires the `van_id` question entirely and rests on `orders.event_id`, which is **0% null across all 65 orders** — stamped by `place_order_atomic` on every path, unlike `van_id`.

- **`eventsMap` WAS KEYED BY DATE AND MISLABELLING REAL ORDERS.** `if (!eventsMap[ev.event_date])` meant **first event on a date wins**, so on a two-event date every order from the second event was labelled with the **first** event's venue — in the on-screen history and in both CSV exports. Not "collapsed": wrong. Re-keyed to event id, with a date-keyed fallback retained so orders with a null `event_id` label exactly as before. **A fix, not a refactor**, and the same class as the recorded `id` (per-event display number) vs `order_key` confusion.

- **🔴 A STALE-PROPS CLASS, FOUND IN THE COMPONENT THAT HAD PATCHED AROUND IT THREE TIMES.** `AddOrderPanel` did `useState(todayEvent)` — a mount-time private copy — re-synced only when the event **id** changed. An override flipping on the **same** event changed no id, so the sync early-returned and the copy stayed stale; and the panel never remounts because it is hidden via CSS to preserve the basket. **Twenty lines below sat an effect whose only job was patching `status` through the same hole. This was the third field to fall through it.** Fixed by deriving `liveEvent` — identity from the operator's selection, values from the freshest available source — as a `const` on every render, with no effect and no dependency array. The `status` effect became genuinely redundant and was **removed**. ⚠️ Resolving against the parent prop alone would have been wrong: a Saturday phone pre-order taken on Friday would have got **Friday's** payment settings.

- **THE DASHBOARD'S EVENT AND TAB NOW PERSIST IN THE URL.** `?event=<uuid>` and `?tab=`, both falling through to the existing defaults on anything unrecognised — a foreign, deleted, cancelled, past or malformed value behaves exactly as no param at all. Ownership is validated by **membership in a server-scoped list**, never by trusting the id. ⚠️ **ONE `replaceState` effect keyed on both**, not two — two effects mutating the same URL in one commit work only by React's ordering and are silently fragile. `replaceState`, not `router.replace`: a pure address-bar rewrite with no navigation, no re-render and no refetch.

- **WRITES NOW RETURN WHAT THEY WROTE.** The two override handlers return the updated row and the client patches state from the response. ⚠️ Two deliberate departures from the obvious implementation, both avoiding recorded hazards: **`select('*')` rather than a named list** (a named select naming a missing column fails the whole statement with `42703` — the silent-empty-board class), and **no `.single()`** (it throws `PGRST116` on zero rows, turning a harmless no-op into a 500 for a write that simply matched nothing). **This is not the flip-back class:** those bugs set optimistic state *before* commit, leaving a window where the client held a value the server did not. Here the value arrives in a post-commit response — nothing is guessed, so nothing needs reverting.

- **THE TRUCK-LEVEL STALENESS SELF-HEALS — RESOLVED, NOT FLAGGED A THIRD TIME.** An eight-link chain, all in source and confirmed against the live publication: Manage saves → `update_truck` → writes the `trucks` row → the dashboard's `postgres_changes` subscription on that row → `reseedRef` → `fetchAll(pin, true)` → `forceSeed` opens the gate → `setTruck` runs. **`setTruck` was NOT moved**, and moving it would have been actively harmful: ungating it makes `truck` a new object every poll, re-running every effect that depends on it including the sound seed that protects Gusto's settings.

- **🔴 THE SUPABASE REALTIME PUBLICATION CONTAINS EXACTLY TWO TABLES: `orders` AND `trucks`.** A `truck_vans` subscription existed in the dashboard and **had never fired**, because the table is not published — and its stated main case had moved out from under it when `online_paused_until` relocated to `truck_events`. **Dead twice over, deleted.** Nothing was lost: the 60s poll calls the identical handler, and the acting device is already instant via `markPending`.

- **`truck_vans` MUST NEVER BE PUBLISHED.** `last_heartbeat_at` lives on that table and is UPDATEd **every 15 seconds per device**. `postgres_changes` filters by **row, not by column**, so there is no way to watch `paused_until` while ignoring `last_heartbeat_at` — publishing it would make every heartbeat from every van fire a full `/api/dashboard` refetch on every connected dashboard, scaling with devices × vans. Cross-device van pause therefore propagates in ≤60s, and that is **accepted, not a gap**. If instant propagation is ever wanted, the prerequisite is moving `last_heartbeat_at` off the table, not publishing it.

- **CASH WAS DE-NESTED FROM THE PAID STEP AND THEN RE-NESTED, ON A LAYOUT ARGUMENT.** The de-nesting reasoning — *"they answer different questions: WHEN do we take money vs HOW does it arrive"* — was true and was **the wrong test**. Two settings can answer different questions and still have one depend on the other, and structure should show the **dependency**. The dependency is real and driven by layout: with the paid step off, one tap means "paid AND collected", so splitting it into Cash/Card would make each button also collect — and the honest label `Cash & collected` does not fit a 72px label box at the 240px KDS column. **There is no honest way to render the split when the button also collects.**

- **SETTINGS-CARD CONVENTIONS SETTLED.** On the dashboard, each setting is its own card titled by the setting, with dependents nested beneath — so a group label and a grey inner panel were both removed as boxes within boxes with nothing to distinguish. In Manage, three groups share one Order settings card, so the sub-panels and their headings do real work and stay. **`SUBCARD_HEADING` is now a Manage-only token.** And: **per-event scope is a property of the SCREEN, not of each row** — Dashboard Settings is per-event, Manage is truck-wide, and repeating that on every row would read as a box of unrelated exceptions.

## V9.6 — 30 July 2026

Delta over V9.5 — the second batch of the same day. **A live outage on localhost whose cause had been latent for two passes, and whose symptom was a supported behaviour.** Nine dropped query errors found and made loud. **Per-event overrides for both payment settings**, including a reversal of a ruling made two passes earlier. **Sound configuration moved per-device** with Gusto's settings preserved. **The button vocabulary settled** — "Done" became "Collected", blue was retired, and the colour system now has one home. **Two columns added. Still no Stripe: company setup is the blocker, not code.**

- **🔴 THE SILENT-EMPTY-BOARD BUG — the worst symptom-to-cause distance yet.** `/api/dashboard`'s **events** query named `show_paid_step_override` and `takes_cash_override` before their migrations had been applied. PostgREST rejected the query with `42703` — and **the error was destructured away**, so `todayEvents` came back `null`, every `selectedEventId` branch required it non-null, the orders block never ran, and **the route returned HTTP 200 with `orders: []`**. No console error, no failed request, no server log. And an empty board is a **documented, supported state** (§5, "orders are strictly event-scoped"), so **the bug wore legitimate behaviour as a disguise.** It presented as the `Done` → `Collected` rename breaking a status filter; the rename was entirely innocent, and the bucketing compares DB status values only. `show_paid_step_override` had entered that select **two passes earlier and was already committed** — either column alone was sufficient, so the board had been broken since the truck-defaults pass and was only noticed later.

- **🔴 `select('*')` DEGRADES; A NAMED SELECT THROWS.** This asymmetry is the whole hazard. `total_minor`, `deal_savings` and `capacity_ack_at` were all added the same week and **none of them could have caused this**, because the orders and truck queries use `select('*')`. Only the events query names columns explicitly. So the risk is not "a new column" — it is **"a new column named in an explicit select"**. Enumerate those before deploying, every time.

- **NINE DROPPED QUERY ERRORS IN ONE ROUTE, NOT ONE.** The sweep of `/api/dashboard` found **five destructures covering nine queries** with no error capture: `truck_events`, `collection_times`, both `orders` queries, `menu_categories`, `menu_items_db`, `truck_vans`, `demo_sessions`. Only `trucks` and `order_payments` were already correct. All now log, and **each log names the CONSEQUENCE rather than just the failure** — "the board will render EMPTY", "prep secs read 0 and NOTHING counts toward capacity this poll", and so on. ⚠️ **`truck_vans` is the subtlest and runs every poll:** every consumer reads `van?.x ?? default`, so a failed query resolves to *"no capacity limit, no cooking step, no order-ready step"* — **a plausible configuration, not a visible fault.**

- **A dropped error plus a `?? default` consumer produces a plausible configuration, not an error.** This is the general form of the `truck_vans` finding and it also describes `paidStepFor`, which falls back to truck defaults when its event lookup fails — silently ignoring any per-event override. Harmless today only because both defaults are `false`; **the first operator to enable cash for one event would get card-only behaviour server-side with no signal anywhere.** Both now log.

- **ON LOCALHOST, THE WORKING TREE *IS* THE DEPLOY.** Code goes live the moment it is saved, ahead of any migration — so a "run the migration before deploying" classification is violated by default during development. That is how a correctly-classified deploy-coupled migration still broke the board. **Third time this week that migration-before-deploy has bitten, and each time it presented as something else.**

- **BOTH PAYMENT SETTINGS NOW HAVE PER-EVENT OVERRIDES.** `truck_events.show_paid_step_override` and `truck_events.takes_cash_override` — both nullable, **nullable-means-inherit, resolved at read time, NO bulk write and NO seeding at event creation.** ⚠️ This is a **deliberate divergence from `order_ready_override`**, which bulk-writes every existing event when the truck default changes and thereby wipes overrides the operator set on purpose. Fine for pause; wrong for "when do we take money" — an operator who set one event to take payment at order must not lose it because they changed their general default a week later. Because nothing is seeded, **an override never carries forward, which is also how it self-expires — no expiry mechanism was built or needed.**

- **`takes_cash` BECAME PER-EVENT, REVERSING A RULING FROM TWO PASSES EARLIER.** It had been settled as truck-level only, on the reasoning that "whether a truck accepts cash is a property of the business, not of a pitch". That reasoning was sound for the case in mind and **incomplete**: if the card terminal fails mid-service, the operator needs cash enabled **for tonight, from the dashboard**, without going into Manage. **"Is this a property of the business or the pitch" is the wrong question when equipment can fail.**

- **ONE RESOLUTION POINT: `lib/payments/paid-step.ts`.** `resolvePaidStep(truck, event)` is the only place either override is resolved, called by all six consumers including the two server-side reads. ⚠️ **`??` and NOT `||`** — an explicit override of `false` must be honoured, not fall through to a `true` default. `||` would treat `false` as "unset" and silently re-inherit; that is the one substitution that looks correct and is wrong, and there is a harness case asserting it for each setting.

- **SOUND CONFIGURATION IS NOW PER-DEVICE, VIA localStorage.** Following the `keep_screen_on` precedent and the V9.0 decision — sound is physical, so it belongs to the device, not the business. Key `hg_soundcfg_${token}`. **The mechanism that protected Gusto:** a device with nothing stored seeds from `trucks.sound_config` rather than from a hardcoded default, **and waits for the truck payload to arrive before seeding** — without that second guard, the async window between mount and payload would have silently reset their deliberately-configured `{"order_due":true,"new_orders":"all"}`. Read via a **lazy `useState` initializer, not a `useEffect`**: for a banner a one-frame flash is cosmetic, for sound the artefact would be **audible**. The write failure is logged three ways **and surfaced to the operator** as a toast — `keep_screen_on` wrapped the same write in a swallowed `try{}catch{}`, which is why "I turned it off and it came back" was possible. 🔴 **`trucks.sound_config` is RETAINED as the seed source** — retiring it requires that every device has loaded at least once since the deploy, or a device that has not would seed from nothing.

- **"DONE" BECAME "COLLECTED", AND THE BINDING CONSTRAINT WAS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE.** The DB status is literally `collected`, and "Done" was ambiguous once the button split. `Mark paid & collected` (153px) **clips by 25px** — not in the button's own row, but in the **cooking-gate row**, where it shares space with the `⏳ Waiting` chip and has no horizontal padding of its own. Chosen: **`Paid & collected`**, at 116px **exactly the width of the string it replaces**, so it cannot regress any layout. Split states are `Mark paid` → `Collected`. **Copy only — every status, action and audit literal verified unchanged by count.**

- **THE COLOUR SYSTEM SETTLED, AND BLUE WAS RETIRED.** Blue was introduced for money actions and removed one pass later as foreign to a page whose vocabulary is orange, slate and green. Final: **orange = action (confirm, take money), green = ready (a kitchen state), slate = done.** Cash vs card is a **variant, not a kind**, so it is distinguished by **icon** (`💷` / `💳`) rather than by two near-identical oranges, which would read as a rendering mistake. All three colours live once in `lib/ui-tokens.ts` with their measured contrast ratios, joined by `SUBCARD_HEADING` after four inline copies of one class string appeared across two Settings screens.

- **TWO COLUMNS ADDED:** `truck_events.show_paid_step_override`, `truck_events.takes_cash_override`.

## V9.5 — 30 July 2026

Delta over V9.4 — the **29–30 July payments phase 1a/1b workstream**. Payments went from a design to a working, verified system: **the payment ledger, rollup, audit log and paid step are all built, deployed and confirmed against live data.** Three new silent-failure findings, one of which had been swallowing money-events since the day it shipped. A **documented-and-swept class reopened by the very next field added**, now fixed by inverting its failure mode. A **standing rule about scope** after this planning chat approved a UI change nobody asked for. **Three columns added.** **Status: still NO Stripe account, no Stripe code. Everything below is cash and own-PDQ, which is the point — phase 1 was designed to be provable without Stripe.**

- **🔴 THE IDEMPOTENCY KEY SWALLOWED EVERY CHARGE AFTER THE FIRST.** `collectIdempotencyKey` returned a **constant per order** — `collect:{order_key}` — so a second manual charge hit `23505`, was treated as a successful replay, and **recorded nothing, forever, with no error**. Pay £9.50 → edit up to £15 → tap "Mark £5.50 paid" → silence. The phase-1a migration header had *explicitly rejected* a composite unique index so that "£10 cash now, £5 later" would remain possible; the constant key forbade it anyway. **Design intent and implementation disagreed from day one and nobody noticed, because part-payment had never been exercised.**

- **NO DETERMINISTIC SERVER-DERIVED KEY CLOSES THE PROBLEM, AND THE DETECTOR MATTERS MORE THAN THE KEY.** Two candidate schemes were simulated across seven sequences. A **total**-based key fails on edit-down-refund-edit-up. A **balance**-based key fails on *"paid in full, customer comes back for another round"* — an ordinary hatch transaction, not an edge case. The adopted key is `collect:{order_key}:{paidBefore}:{balance}` (a state-transition key), which passes everything except the refund cycle. **That residue is not fixable with any deterministic key: if the key is a function of ledger state, any sequence returning the ledger to an earlier state and repeating the same transition must collide.** The complete answer is a client-minted per-tap key — `op_id` already exists in the outbox and is never transmitted. **So the real safety property is the DETECTOR:** a swallowed duplicate where the balance FELL is a genuine replay (silent, correct); a swallowed duplicate where the balance is UNCHANGED is a real collision (throws, surfaces as `paymentWarning` + a loud log + `ledger_failed: true`). It does not depend on the key scheme, and it would have caught this very bug on the first part-payment.

- **🔴 A NEW SILENT-FAILURE MEMBER — two different outcomes sharing one return shape.** `recordCollectionPayment` returned `{inserted: false, chargedMinor: 0}` for BOTH "already recorded" and "nothing outstanding". No caller branched on it. So the handler returned 200, the operator saw success, and **the audit log recorded a successful action that moved no money.** The information was technically present and structurally unusable.

- **🔴 THE PROJECTION-OMISSION CLASS WAS DOCUMENTED THREE TIMES, SWEPT AND CLOSED IN V9.0 — AND REOPENED BY THE NEXT FIELD ADDED.** `/api/dashboard` returned a hand-maintained include list; `show_paid_step` was not in it, so `data.truck.show_paid_step` was `undefined` and the toggle re-defaulted to `false` on every mount. **The V9.0 warning that "a newly-omitted field reopens the class" was sitting as a comment four lines above the omission.** A warning you must read and remember is not a control. Fixed by **spread-and-redact** — the row is spread and a redact list removes secrets — which **inverts the failure mode**: forgetting a field used to break a feature silently; now the worst case is a leaked field, which is visible and harmless. Verified against the live schema: 88 columns on `trucks`, all assessed, exactly four redacted (`dashboard_token`, `dashboard_pin`, `messenger_page_token`, `kds_pin`), zero false positives. **`takes_cash` was the first setting added after the fix and it reached the client with no map edit — the fix did what it was for.**

- **TWO HYPOTHESES EXCLUDED, RECORDED SO THEY ARE NOT RE-CHASED.** (1) **A whole-object save CANNOT re-default a column** — PostgREST `UPDATE` writes only keys present in the object, so "send only changed fields" is already true everywhere. (2) **The realtime handler refetches rather than merging a payload**, so it cannot clobber local state. Both were asserted by the planning chat and both were wrong.

- **PAYMENT LEDGER, ROLLUP AND AUDIT LOG — BUILT, DEPLOYED, VERIFIED LIVE.** `order_payments` (integer minor units only, idempotency key, RLS-no-policy) **[CORRECTED V11.4 — this previously read "no FK cascade concerns pending", which was ambiguous and was read as "there is no FK cascade". THERE ARE TWO, BOTH `ON DELETE CASCADE`: `order_key → orders` and `truck_id → trucks`. See §16 and §27.]** with `recalcOrderPayment` as the ONLY writer of `payment_status` and `amount_paid`. `action_audit_log` — append-only, **no foreign keys by design** so rows outlive their subject, following `allergen_audit_log`. Actor attribution verified resolving to `owner` + a real name on web. Live-verified end to end: collect → undo → re-collect leaves three audit rows, the undo's `before_state` carrying the full deleted ledger row including its idempotency key.

- **THE WRITE PATH DISCARDED AN IDENTITY IT ALREADY HAD.** `/api/dashboard/action`'s entire auth was `verifyToken(token, pin)` — no cookie, no `getUser`, no `truck_users` read — while the sibling GET route resolved name, role and membership in full and the browser displayed it. **The read path knew who you were; the write path never asked.** Fixed with one shared resolver, split into `resolveActor` (may throw, GET, preserved byte-for-byte) and `resolveActorSafe` (action route). ⚠️ **A blanket try/catch around the GET resolver would have converted a genuine auth failure into a silent success**, letting a foreign operator through during an auth outage — caught before shipping.

- **THE PAID STEP.** `trucks.show_paid_step` (**column** default false; ⚠️ **"Gusto unaffected" was WRONG — corrected V11.6: Gusto is `show_paid_step` TRUE**, and three of twelve trucks are) splits "Mark paid and done" into a relabelling single button: unpaid → `Mark paid`, paid → `Done`, part-paid → `Mark £X.XX paid`. **No double-tap gesture** — one tap advances a stage, so two quick taps do both with no timing window, no debounce and no delayed first action. `trucks.takes_cash` (default false) splits the paid action into `💷 Cash` / `💳 Card`, one tap either way, recording `order_payments.method`. 🔴 **AND SINCE V11.25 THE PLAIN BUTTONS WRITE IT TOO: `takes_cash` is a DECLARATION** — a live, labelled control ("Do you take cash?") — **so a truck with it OFF has said it is card-only, and a plain "Mark paid" / "Mark paid & collected" there records `method:'card'`.** With it ON the plain names are not what the card renders, nothing is sent, and the value stays NULL — **the PAYMENT-NOT-RECORDED repair must never fabricate a method nobody was asked for.** `collected` honours `body.method` from V11.25; **it hardcoded NULL before, so a one-press truck could never record one whatever it tapped.** ⚠️ **The toasts now name it, reusing PaymentActionsModal's own phrases — "paid in cash" / "paid on your card machine" — one vocabulary across modal and toast.** **`method` is a SEPARATE axis from `channel`** — `channel` answers "does the 0.99% apply and does this count toward the allowance", and cash and own-PDQ are identical on it. Widening `channel` would make every fee query an `in (...)` over a growing list, and one forgotten member silently charges a fee on cash.

- **`default_walkup_payment` WAS ADDED AND REMOVED WITHIN A DAY.** A truck-level default for "walk-ups usually pay at order / at collection" is wrong about half the time, because walk-ups and phone orders arrive through the SAME panel with OPPOSITE timings — so the operator must check and flip on every order anyway, which is worse than no default. Replaced with **two equal confirm actions, neither remembered**: `Confirm order` and `Cash £X` / `Card £X`. This is open-check semantics and matches how a POS actually behaves.

- **THE CAPACITY WARNING WAS CORRECT AND THE OPERATOR ACTION WAS LEGITIMATE.** Closing the 28 July investigation: window 18:15–18:20 genuinely held 4 pizzas against a ceiling of 2, and `van_id IS NULL` + `items[0].cartKey` proved two of the three contributing orders were **operator walk-ups**, which bypass all capacity gating by design. No defect. The display was the problem, and `❗` now marks strictly-over slots.

- **A STANDING RULE, AFTER BREAKING IT.** *Do not change UI the operator did not ask about.* An instruction to "make Ready match the toggles" could not be satisfied without changing the toggles; the coding chat flagged that prominently and then **resolved it itself in the direction that expanded scope**, and this planning chat approved it. Flagging is not a substitute for stopping. See §35.

- **THREE COLUMNS ADDED:** `trucks.show_paid_step`, `trucks.takes_cash`, `order_payments.method`.

## V9.4 — 29 July 2026

Delta over V9.3 — the **28–29 July payments-foundation workstream**. Two themes. First, **a read-before-building pass on payments turned into a schema-truth audit**: four columns the manual and the code disagreed about, in both directions, all on `orders`/`operators`. Second, **a live customer-ordering outage caused by a migration that reported success and did nothing** — a new and nastier member of the recorded-as-applied family. **Step zero shipped** (server-authoritative pricing, price-lock on edits, integer minor units). **The capacity investigation closed with no defect found** — the warning was correct and the display was not. **Three columns added and verified in production.** **The payments commercial model is now locked** (new §37). **Status: Stripe Connect is NOT built and no Stripe account exists. Step zero is committed (`5208cbe`), migrations applied, deployed, customer path verified.**

- **🔴 A NEW FAILURE CLASS — *present-but-never-written*.** `orders.source` **exists** (text, default `'web'`, CHECK `web|manual|whatsapp`) and **nothing has ever written it**: all 356 rows read `'web'` by default, including walk-ups. Order channel is instead inferred from `customer_email IS NULL` (`app/api/manage/route.ts:1248-1249`), whose own comment claims *"No source/is_manual column exists yet"* — it does exist, it was just always empty. The inference misclassifies **walk-ups where the operator captured an email for a receipt** as online, always in that one direction. This is worse than a phantom column: a phantom throws `42703` and you know immediately, while a defaulted column returns a plausible value on every row and reads as data. **It misled this planning chat into a wrong conclusion about which orders an operator had placed.**

- **🔴 `create or replace function` SUCCEEDING PROVES THE SQL PARSED, NOT THAT IT WORKS.** PL/pgSQL resolves column references at **execution**, not creation. A function body naming a column that does not exist applies cleanly, reports success, and then throws `42703` on the first real call. On 28 July this took **customer ordering down for ~15 minutes on a live trading evening** (Gusto, Belchamp, 17:00–20:00). **A function that references a column is not applied until a probe has executed it.** See §35.

- **FULL-FILE PASTE INTO THE SUPABASE SQL EDITOR CAN SILENTLY RUN NOTHING.** The same migration's `add column if not exists` statements *and* its function block were both skipped while the editor reported success. **Run `create or replace function` blocks ALONE, in an empty tab**, and verify with `pg_get_functiondef(...) like '%new_column%'`.

- **CUSTOMER-PATH OUTAGES ARE INVISIBLE FROM THE OPERATOR SIDE — second instance.** Walk-ups use a **direct insert**; customer orders use **`place_order_atomic`**. During the outage the operator dashboard was fully functional. This is the §65 shape exactly. Recovery check: `increment_event_order_counter` advances *before* the insert, so **a rolled-back order permanently consumes its display number** — gaps in the sequence are the fingerprint of failed attempts. (Verified none: counter 15, highest order 15, 15 saved.)

- **FOUR SCHEMA CORRECTIONS.** (1) **`operators.stripe_customer_id` DOES NOT EXIST** — asserted by V3 §13 and §16 and never true. (2) **`operators.billing` DOES NOT EXIST** — same. (3) **`orders.payment_status` and `orders.amount_paid` DO exist and were undocumented** — `payment_status` text default `'unpaid'` with CHECK `unpaid|paid|refunded|failed`; `amount_paid` numeric(8,2), unpopulated on all 346 rows. (4) **The §16 `orders` entry listed ten columns for a thirty-two-column table** and read as exhaustive — which is how `payment_status` stayed invisible to both the planning chat and the coding chat for two months.

- **MONEY IS SAFE BY ACCIDENT: POSTGRES IS THE ROUNDING LAYER.** `orders.total`, `subtotal`, `discount_amt`, `amount_paid` are all **`numeric(8,2)`**, so the JS float error (`12.20 + 0.10 = 12.299999999999999`, reproducible from `lib/order-calculations.ts`'s own composition rule) is annihilated at the insert boundary. Verified: **0 of 346 rows** exceed 2dp. `round(total * 100)` is therefore exact. This shrank step zero considerably — but it is protection nobody designed, and it caps a single order at £999,999.99.

- **THE DEAL AND DISCOUNT DIVERGENCES ARE LATENT, NOT LIVE.** **Zero** orders in production have ever carried a deal, a `discount_code`, or a non-zero `discount_amt`. So the known incoherences (`total ≠ subtotal − discount_amt` when deals are present; `AddOrderPanel` shipping `dealSavings` into the `discountAmt` slot) are traps waiting for the first operator to switch deals on, not data to repair.

- **🔴 THE CUSTOMER-PATH PRICE VALIDATION IS A NO-OP AND STILL IS.** `calculateOrderTotal` reads `item.price`; the customer page posts `unit_price`. The multiplication yields `NaN`, every `Math.abs(submitted − NaN) > tolerance` comparison returns `false`, and **the guard passes unconditionally** — client-supplied totals have been stored verbatim since the path was written. `[ORDER VALIDATION]` has never logged because it cannot. **NOT FIXED** — see §27. Under price-lock this is now the single point where a price becomes authoritative for the life of an order, including any refund derived from it.

- **PRICE IS LOCKED AT PLACEMENT (new rule).** Once an order is placed its prices are frozen; a later menu change applies only to future orders. Existing lines re-price from the **stored order row**, matched by item name + modifier-name set; only genuinely **new** lines take the current menu price. This reversed a same-day design decision that had re-priced everything from the live menu. Note the stored shape supports a stricter variant (per-modifier prices are stored, so `lockedBase = unit_price − Σ modifiers[].price` is exact) — **not built**; today an existing item whose modifiers change re-prices its whole line.

- **STEP ZERO BUILT AND DEPLOYED (`5208cbe`).** Server-authoritative re-pricing on the operator edit path (client `unit_price` is now advisory only); `discount_amt` recomputed **and written** on edit; `dealSavings` moved to its own column so `discount_amt` means money-deducted everywhere; the edit handler now checks its own `.update()` result instead of returning `{success:true}` unconditionally; `lib/slot-bookings.ts` returns its write errors. **Verified in production: a £9.50 customer order wrote `total_minor` 950.**

- **THE CAPACITY WARNING WAS CORRECT — THE DISPLAY WAS NOT.** Window 18:15–18:20 genuinely held 4 pizzas against a ceiling of 2. No engine defect. But the banner named `18:20` (a collection time at which nothing is over), named order `#10` by **string-matching its collection slot rather than its contribution** (`lib/capacity-breach.ts:86,:107`) — and #10 was the only innocent party, a 2-pizza order at a 2-pizza ceiling flagged because two operator walk-ups at 18:30 reach backward into its window. `over_total` and `over_cats` are computed, shipped to the browser, and read only by the dismiss-signature function.

- **FULL IS NOT OVER.** `buildSlotIndicators` exposed only `tone`, which goes red at `concurrency >= ceiling`, so an at-capacity slot and an over-subscribed one were **indistinguishable**. `overTotal` added to the returned interface; **`❗` marks strictly-over slots only**, in both pickers, permanently — it does not clear on acknowledgement.

- **THREE COLUMNS ADDED, ALL DEPLOY-COUPLED, ALL VERIFIED LIVE.** `orders.total_minor` (integer — authoritative charge amount in pence), `orders.deal_savings` (numeric(8,2)), `orders.capacity_ack_at` (timestamptz, **server-minted**). Migrations `20260728_orders_total_minor_deal_savings.sql` and `20260728_orders_capacity_ack.sql`.

- **THE OVER-CAPACITY CONFIRM MODAL IS REBUILT AT SUBMIT.** A richer slot-select modal existed and was deleted 15 June (`448130f`, *"operator-only friction"*; tombstone at `AddOrderPanel.tsx:636-643`). It read the **stale** `capacityInputs` cache — which has no poll and no realtime invalidation — which is why it warned about slots that were fine. The rebuild keeps the **submit-time** trigger and its `cache:'no-store'` fetch, and now uses `fit.bound_by` (previously computed and discarded) for the copy. Note `consider()` keeps the **first** red and the per-category loop runs first, so a category bind wins over the global ceiling.

- **NEW §37 — the payments commercial model, locked.** Rates, allowance, trial suppression, the payment ledger design, Connect account shape, currency/country rules, and the Tap-to-Pay platform constraint.

## V9.3 — 28 July 2026

Delta over V9.2 — the **native-throw remediation**, later the same day. One theme: **a finding that survived contact with its own evidence, and a mechanism that did not.** V9.2's §35 native-throw invariant is **strengthened** (it is framework-level, not push-specific), while the **severity ratings built on top of it are withdrawn** — the null-`getActivity()` path they assumed does not exist. **One new §35 invariant.** **One §35 entry corrected and its sweep recounted.** **A §36 VERIFICATION STATUS block**, because the gap between *built*, *reasoned* and *observed* had stopped being legible. **Two §27 items.** **Status: unchanged — no Android build has shipped, no store listing exists, and the full order-flow click-through remains unrun on either platform since V6.3.**

- **§35 GAINED ONE INVARIANT — the fail-closed/fail-open pair.** `device_notification_prefs` reads a missing row as **ENABLED**; `offlineAlertsEnabled()`'s new catch reads an unreadable pref as **DISABLED**. They are both correct and are **allowed to disagree**, because a stored default encodes **intent** while a runtime fallback encodes **certainty**. Recorded specifically so a later "harmonise these" tidy does not break one of them.

- **§35 NATIVE-THROW ENTRY CORRECTED — mechanism strengthened, severity withdrawn.** The invariant is **framework-level**: `Bridge.callPluginMethod` rethrows any `@PluginMethod` exception as `RuntimeException` on a background `HandlerThread` (`Bridge.java:848-851`), and `executeOnMainThread` is a bare `post()` with **no catch** (`:909-913`) — so it holds for **every** plugin, not just push. But an earlier report's HIGH ratings rested on `getActivity()` returning null, and **`Bridge.java:114` declares it `private final`** — it cannot. `AndroidManifest.xml:13`'s `configChanges` list further removes rotation, fold, split-screen and dark-mode from the reachable states. **Two unknowns are left flagged as unknowns** (whether `getWindow()` can return null; whether flag mutation on a detached Window throws), and **no `guardedInvoke` wrapper was built** — it would have *looked* like protection against native throws while providing none, which is the anti-pattern the invariant itself warns about.

- **SWEEP RECOUNTED: SIXTEEN awaited plugin calls, not ten** — **1 call-site guarded / 15 unguarded**, of which **12 sit behind an ineffective `catch`** and **4 had none at all**. Those four are now caught, for **JS-side rejection and import failure only**, with comments saying so at each site. The earlier "nine behind an ineffective catch" framing was wrong about the two that mattered most.

- **THE REAL FIX WAS A DELETION.** `FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON` is **window-scoped**, not a wake lock we own: backgrounded ⇒ no effect, destroyed ⇒ gone with the Window, recreated ⇒ not even restored. The `allowSleep()` cleanup was therefore redundant on every OS path — and on the dashboard it fired on **every dep change**, making toggle-off a double release and toggle-on a release/re-acquire flicker. Removed from both screens. **The resulting navigation delta is INTENDED and is now recorded inline at both sites:** keep-awake is a **DEVICE preference**, meaning *"this screen stays on"*, not *"stays on while looking at orders"*.

- **§16 GAINED A CLOSED QUESTION.** `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` is **not** in our manifest — it arrives by **manifest merge** from `@capacitor/local-notifications`. `@capacitor/push-notifications` declares no permissions and relies on it, so **removing local-notifications would silently strip the permission from push as well.**

## V9.2 — 28 July 2026

Delta over V9.1 — the **27–28 July Android + demo/onboarding workstream**. One theme: the second native platform stopped being a theoretical port and started producing findings, most of which are **not Android-specific** — they are asymmetries that only became visible once a second platform existed. **Eleven new §35 invariants** (native throws pass through JS `try`/`catch`; one owner per safe-area inset; two APIs fronting one OS grant do not report it equally; a repo inside a synced folder gets conflict copies; a ported permission bypass without its routing branch widens access; an unordered first-row pick is non-deterministic; native tooling enforces filename/content rules the web never does). **Three corrections to existing entries.** **Two notification-preference migrations APPLIED**; a third **written and deliberately NOT run**. A new **§36 Android platform** section. **Status: the Android client half of push is VERIFIED end to end (a real FCM token on a real device); the SERVER half is not wired. No Android build has shipped and no store listing exists.**

- **§35 GAINED ELEVEN INVARIANTS — seven with a sweep status** per the standing rule. The two that cost the most time: **a JS `try`/`catch` around a Capacitor plugin call does not protect against a native throw** (there is no promise to reject — `PushNotificationsPlugin.register()` killed the process from inside a wrapped call), and **only one mechanism may own a safe-area inset** (Capacitor 8 pads the WebView on API 35+ *and* zeroes `env()`, so adding CSS padding recreates the two-band bug V8.7 removed on iOS).

- **THREE CORRECTIONS.** (1) V8.6 recorded `20260701_van_devices.sql` and `20260701_van_notification_prefs.sql` as **PENDING**; both are **APPLIED** (verified 27 July) — *recorded-as-pending, actually-applied*, the **inverse** of the §65 incident and the same class. (2) The "native token-only access defaults `userRole` to `'owner'`" note read as a general property of the native shell; it is **the MANAGE page's client-side `|| 'owner'` fallback**. `/api/dashboard` runs ONE role block for both cookie and Bearer, so a staff member on the native app correctly resolves to `'staff'`. (3) `lib/native/statusBar.ts` carried **three verified no-ops on modern Android** plus a hardcoded colour matching nothing in the brand — **a native helper written for one platform must be re-verified against the other, not assumed.**

- **NOTIFICATION PREFERENCES — `device_notification_prefs` APPLIED.** Per-device, per-type, replacing an accidental three-way split (per-VAN `van_notification_prefs`; the not-per-type `van_devices.notify_enabled`; device-local Capacitor Preferences the server cannot see and therefore cannot use to gate a push). **27 rows across 9 devices, verified.** `20260728_notification_prefs_retire_old_stores.sql` is **WRITTEN and DELIBERATELY NOT RUN** — it drops both old stores while `app/api/orders/submit/route.ts` still reads them. Both left **DORMANT** per the leave-dormant-then-sweep precedent. See §16.

- **§36 ANDROID PLATFORM created.** Capacitor 8 remote-URL shell shared with iOS; `android/**` inert on web and living on `main` per the V8.8 rule; **the UA marker is a per-platform config key, not a property of being native** — adding a platform means adding the marker or the V8.7 login loop returns; **Android push is FCM while iOS stays pure APNs, which makes `van_devices.platform` load-bearing**; and **iOS has never been capable of registering for push** — there is no `.entitlements` file and no `aps-environment` key.

- **⚠️ THE LANDING PAGE NOW STATES ANDROID IS AVAILABLE. IT IS NOT.** No build has shipped; no store listing exists. Recorded as a **CLAIM AHEAD OF THE PRODUCT** — the same class as the V9.0 *gate-enabled and advertised ≠ built* lesson. `/landing` is `noindex` but **not access-gated**, and is linked from the legal pages and the demo-return bounce. Deliberate forward commitment; a debt with a date, not a description of the software.

- **THE DEMO EVENT ROLL IS DELETED, AND AN ELAPSED DEMO NOW ENDS.** `rollDemoEventIfStale` shifted an elapsed demo forward on every dashboard load, and all three of its faults were confirmed against live data: it **wrote order slots directly, bypassing the seeder**, clamping overshoots onto the final slot (**15 orders on `23:59`**, breaching the per-slot mains ceiling the seeder guarantees); it preserved a compressed board's distribution **forever**; and it shifted **the visitor's own test order** — one placed at 23:40 reappeared at 09:45 the next morning. Replaced by an explicit **"Start a new service"** (`lib/demo-restart.ts`): a truck-wide wipe, a fresh window, a re-seed. ⚠️ **Truck-wide, not date-scoped** — `provisionDemoEvent(replaceExisting)` deletes by `event_date`, which would sail straight past yesterday's event. Full detail in the onboarding spec §10 Phase 2E.

- **SEEDED ORDER COUNT SCALES WITH WINDOW LENGTH — which also fixed the stride collapse.** The count was a constant regardless of window, so `stride = slots.length / budgets.length` hit **1** once a window fell to ≤~16 bookable slots: every slot got a budget and the taper flattened into a solid block. A **threshold effect, not gradual degradation** — the reason late-night demos looked broken while midday ones looked right. Scaling the target to bookable slots (`ORDERS_PER_SLOT ≈ 1.057`) keeps stride > 1 at every size. Before the fix a 5-slot window placed 14 of 37 and **silently dropped 23**.

- **SIGNUP COPY CENTRALISED into one variant-keyed object** (`upload` / `sample` / `saveOnly`) with a **deliberate upload/sample divergence** — someone who uploaded their own menu has an artifact worth naming, a sample visitor does not, so "save my menu" would be false for them. Sibling keys with identical shapes, so editing one shows the others unchanged in the same diff hunk. The `/api/dashboard` **`demo` block** supplies the variant and **retires the `?welcome=sample` param**, which survived exactly one navigation. **`canSetup` is now admin-aware** so the signup chain can be walked on production without opening signup publicly — not a client-trusted flag: `/api/signup` re-reads the session server-side and checks `operators.is_admin`.

- **`extraction_source` MIGRATION RECONCILED.** The column was written and read by code and present in production, but **in no migration file** — see §35's "a swallowed write makes a missing column indistinguishable from a working one". Now written as `add column if not exists`, a deliberate no-op against prod.

> **STATUS FOR THIS ENTRY.** **VERIFIED LIVE:** the scraper fixes — rule-detection loop, day-of-week learner disabled, failure visibility. **BUILT BUT UNVERIFIED:** all of the demo and signup work above, and the Android work. The Android client half of push is the one native thing verified end to end; its server half is not wired.

- **§27 GAINED FIVE ITEMS**, one of which is a blocker on another: the **iOS billing / App Store decision** (three options, all governed by an unverified question about whether an IAP obligation exists at all), the **notification honesty pass** (whose one-time `hg_notify_*` client migration MUST ship in the same release as the Settings card), the **FCM sender**, **Android hardware back**, and the **notification icon**.

## V9.1 — 24 July 2026

Delta over V9.0 — the **23–24 July onboarding session**. One theme: closing the gap between "a stranger lands on `/landing`" and "a working truck with a menu and a schedule". **Signup moved INTO the demo modal** (a two-step wizard over endpoints that already existed), the **import wizard made setup-aware** via a single `inSetup` flag, a **schedule step** added after the menu commit, and a batch of **demo-reliability fixes** (fixed-length event window, now-aware seeded orders, a roll that re-derives from the same rule, commit-menu read batching, `maxDuration`). **§35 "Cross-cutting engineering invariants" created**; live-schema facts added to **§16**; the onboarding backlog added to **§27**. **Status: the SIGNUP CHAIN was verified end to end on 24 July. Everything else in this entry is BUILT but UNVERIFIED.**

- **SIGNUP MOVED INTO THE DEMO MODAL — orchestration, not new contracts.** A **two-step wizard** inside the demo modal drives endpoints that already existed, in order: **`/api/signup` → `signInWithPassword` → `update-profile` → `create_truck` → `update_settings`**. **No endpoint contracts changed** — the wizard is a caller, not a new API surface, so the pre-existing signup path is untouched. **`/setup`'s identity step is BYPASSED on this path** — the wizard already collected that identity, and asking again is the same question twice. **VERIFIED END TO END on 24 July** — the only part of this session that has been.

- **IMPORT WIZARD IS SETUP-AWARE — one flag, `inSetup` (`setup_step != null && setup_step !== 'done'`).** That single derived predicate unlocks four behaviours: **stepper continuity** (the import wizard renders as part of the setup progression, not as a standalone tool), a **finish-later exit**, **reworded Settings references** (a brand-new operator has no Settings page in their head yet), and a fix to the **unconditional "allergens aren't set" notice**, which fired regardless of state. **Every one of these is GATED on `inSetup`, so an existing operator's import is unaffected.** The gate is the point: this is a new *mode* of an existing wizard, not a rewrite of it.

- **SCHEDULE STEP — after the menu commit, SETUP-MODE ONLY.** **Three routes:** a **verified URL**, a **photo import**, or a **manual date** — all three **reuse the existing ScheduleTab flows** rather than forking a second schedule implementation. **⚠️ Scraper enrolment (`schedule_url` + `scraper_preference: 'auto'`) is written ONLY on a SUCCESSFUL Verify**, never on a pasted-but-unverified URL. Enrolling an unverified URL hands the scraper a target it can't read and produces a truck that looks scheduled and never is — and a consistent under-read reads as "reliable" (see the scrape-frequency notes).

- **DEMO RELIABILITY BATCH.**
  - **FIXED-LENGTH EVENT WINDOW** — half-hour floor, **3h** long, **clamped at midnight**. One rule, one place.
  - **NOW-AWARE SEEDED-ORDER FLOOR** — seeded demo orders can no longer land behind the current time.
  - **THE ROLL RE-DERIVES FROM THE SAME RULE** — the roll doesn't reimplement the window, it recomputes it, and **recovers closed events** rather than leaving a demo stranded.
  - **`commitMenu` READ BATCHING — 143 → 85 round trips.**
  - **`maxDuration` SET ON `/api/demo`** — it inherited the ~10–15s platform default against a 40–45s workload, so it **had never worked deployed** (recorded as an invariant in §35).
  - **HONEST-FAILURE + SLOW-WAIT UX** — a failing demo says so instead of hanging; a slow one says it's slow. Same principle as the wake-lock toggle: never show a state you aren't delivering.
  - **TEMPLATE-CARRYOVER GUARD.**

- **§35 "CROSS-CUTTING ENGINEERING INVARIANTS" CREATED.** Lessons that belong to no single subsystem and had nowhere to live: the **`position: fixed` inside a transformed ancestor** trap, **a route that blocks for tens of seconds must declare its own `maxDuration`**, **a timeout set inside a call's normal latency range is a truncation** (and never retry an abort), **wiring is not data flow** — verify the WRITE separately from the read (`demo_sessions.extraction` had a column, a read, a route and a UI, and no writer), **verify the cascade you actually depend on, not an adjacent one**, and **a flag named for a behaviour is not proof of that behaviour**.

- **§16 + §27 UPDATED.** **Live-schema facts** added to §16 (verified against the live schema, not inferred). **Onboarding backlog** added to §27.

A truck-wide setting forces the counter iPad and the owner's pocket phone to agree when they shouldn't.** Offline-protection is unaffected (`toggleOfflineProtection` reads runtime state, not the column). **THE BANNER RULE:** shows iff *(device pref ON, read synchronously)* AND *(lock not held)* — pref OFF → never (no flash); native → held from launch → never.

- **WAKE-LOCK ACTIVATION — properly fixed (SUPERSEDES the V8.9 item-3 gesture mechanics below).** Measured on tablet Safari: the "tap anywhere" banner FAILED, then the header toggle SUCCEEDED on the *same tap, seconds later*. **MECHANISM: `pointerdown` vs `click`, not the async gap.** The old banner had no handler; acquisition rode a **global one-shot listener on `pointerdown`/`touchend`/`keydown`**. `pointerdown` fires FIRST in the tap sequence and consumed the single shot — and **WebKit does NOT grant a user-activation for `wakeLock.request` on a bare `pointerdown`** (the *start* of a gesture, which could still become a scroll/drag); it grants it on the **completed** gesture — `click`, which the real `<button>` toggle fired. Chrome honours `pointerdown` too, so it read as Safari-only. **The async gap was NOT the cause** — the working toggle already `await`ed `getPlugin()` *before* the request and still succeeded, proving a microtask of an already-resolved promise doesn't spend Safari's transient activation — but it was closed anyway as hygiene. **THE FIX (`lib/native/keepAwake.ts` + dashboard/KDS):** (1) `KeepAwakePrompt` is now a **real `<button>`** reading **"Keep screen on"** whose `onClick` runs the **same** acquire path as the toggle (`onAcquire → applyKeepScreenOn(true) → keepAwake()`) — a `click` WebKit honours; (2) the **global gesture listener is removed** entirely (`armGestureAcquire` gone — an unreliable pointerdown request is exactly what failed); (3) `keepAwake()` reordered so `navigator.wakeLock.request('screen')` runs with **nothing awaited before it** — `isNativePlatform()` is a *synchronous* check and the only `await import()` lives on the native branch; (4) `keepAwakeOnGesture()` → **`prepareKeepAwake()`** (mount / pref-restore): native acquires immediately, web only sets intent + reflects state (no auto-request, no listener). Success/failure still flow through the existing `subscribeWakeState` binary toggle. ⚠️ **Verify on tablet SAFARI over https — the whole bug is Safari's stricter activation model; Chrome and native cannot prove it.**

- **⚠️ APP-LOCK HARD LOCKOUT — the near-miss that would have shipped to an operator (fix committed, branch `app-lock-fix`).** Enabling Touch ID **locked Dominic out of the app entirely** on the physical iPad. Two distinct defects, **both in the surrounding re-lock handler** — the biometric call itself was **textbook** (all four `@aparajita/capacitor-biometric-auth` v10 options correct; the resolve-on-success / throw-on-failure contract read right):
  - **THE LOOP.** On real iOS, presenting the Face/Touch ID prompt makes the app **resign-active**, and dismissing it — **INCLUDING ON SUCCESS** — makes it **become-active** → `appStateChange{isActive:true}` → the `onAppResume` handler `setLocked(true)` + `attempt()` → prompt again. Infinite. It was **`authenticate()`'s OWN lifecycle churn feeding the re-lock**, not a genuine background→foreground.
  - **NO ESCAPE HATCH (worse).** The in-prompt device-passcode fallback didn't help — entering it dismisses the prompt the same way success does, feeding the same loop. The only "off" switch lives in `OperatorDeviceConfig`, **inside the app**. Circular. **A biometric lock with no bypass = permanent lockout on a live-service device** (wet hands, a cut finger, a dead sensor = can't take orders at all).
  - **FIX — two parts.** (1) `authInProgress` ref, **CONSUME-ON-RESUME**: the become-active event *itself* clears the guard — **NOT a `setTimeout`** (a clock can be raced by a slow device; an event can't). A *later*, genuine foreground still re-locks, so the feature survives. (2) A **mandatory BACKUP PIN set at enable time** — you **cannot enable app-lock without one**, and that requirement is what actually closes the lockout. **PBKDF2-SHA256, 100k iterations + 16-byte salt** via Web Crypto (no bcrypt in a webview), stored hashed in native **Preferences**; auto-surfaced after 2 failed/cancelled biometric attempts.
  - **WHY A PIN, NOT THE ACCOUNT PASSWORD.** The password needs **network**. An operator whose prompt won't present at a rural venue with no signal would still be locked out — **exactly the scenario the app exists for**. A fallback that fails offline isn't a fallback. The PIN is a Preferences read + a local hash: **no network, no biometric, no plugin** — it mirrors iOS's own Face ID + passcode pairing.
  - **⚠️ RESIDUAL to watch:** consume-on-resume assumes the dismissal fires **exactly ONE** become-active. If a device fires two, the second re-locks and the loop returns → **needs a debounce on the consume** before this is trusted across more hardware.
  - **ESCAPE IF LOCKED OUT:** Safari Web Inspector → console → `localStorage.removeItem('hg_app_lock')` → reload. A **rebuild / reinstall-over-existing does NOT clear it** (same bundle id keeps its WKWebView data container); **only delete-then-reinstall** does.

- **⚠️ STANDING LESSON — SIMULATOR-VALIDATED ≠ VERIFIED.** The app-lock loop was **simulator-validated and passed**: the simulator's "Matching Face" does **not** reproduce the resign / become-active lifecycle a real Secure Enclave prompt causes. In one afternoon the physical iPad found **THREE** defects the simulator masked — the lockout, the offline slot-picker gap, and the wake-lock activation bug. The manual's **"hardware-gated, unverified"** warnings were pointing at **real defects, not hypotheticals**. **Anything touching a native prompt, the screen, or the network lifecycle is UNVERIFIED until it runs on hardware** — a simulator pass means "compiles," not "works."

- **OFFLINE SLOT PICKER — capacity lights missing offline (found on the device).** Offline, the operator saw slot **times** but **no capacity traffic-lights**: the picker fetches its own **`/api/slots`, which is NOT in the SW cache** (unlike `/api/dashboard`), and its `catch` silently **NULLed `capacityInputs`** → fell to a bare-time fallback. **NOT a deliberate honesty stance** — the day strip (`displaySlots`) already computes **advisory** offline capacity from the cached inputs with an explicit comment sanctioning it; the picker was simply never wired to that path (contrast the events `catch`, which explicitly preserves: "must not wipe the list"). **FIX:** extracted **`buildOfflineOccupancy` into `lib/slot-capacity.ts`** — **ONE shared fold** used by both strip and picker so they can't diverge; the panel derives its inputs (authoritative `/api/slots` when present, else the dashboard's SW-cached `offlineCapacity`). **Plus a reconnect backstop:** the fetch effect is keyed on `manualEvent.id`/date/times, so a panel left **OPEN across a reconnect never refetched** — an **online-transition effect now forces it**. **Offline lights are ADVISORY** (the device can't see customer or other-device orders); the reconnect safety net stays `CapacityBreachBanner` + never-reject replay, unchanged.

So a `<table>` inside an `overflow-x:auto` wrapper becomes its OWN scroll container, and `position:sticky` on the `thead` pins **inside that content-height box** — it never sticks on PAGE scroll. The landing artifact's comparison table had exactly this (`.cmp-wrap{overflow-x:auto}` + a sticky `thead`), so the header silently didn't stick. **FIX: don't use a table + overflow wrapper — mirror Manage → Billing's FLEX layout:** a `sticky top:var(--nav-h)` header row with **fixed narrow columns**. The SAME `--nav-h` variable drives the nav height AND the sticky offset, so they can't desync — no magic pixel offset. And fixed narrow columns **fit mobile with NO horizontal scroll** — which removes the `overflow-x` that creates the trap in the first place. (Same family as the earlier sticky menu-category-header regressions.)
